correctness.rationale: For each integer \(a\geq0\), a reducible monic cubic has an integer root. Translating \(X=Y+a+3\) gives \(y^3=(a+3)(3y+2)\). For odd \(y\), coprimality forces \(3y+2=\pm1\) and \(a+3=1\). For even \(y=2k\), divisibility forces \(3k+1\mid4\) and \(k\in\{-1,0,1\}\), giving \(a+3\in\{2,0,1\}\). All contradict \(a+3\geq3\). The nonzero discriminant is \(108(a+2)(a+3)^2\); the irreducible-cubic discriminant criterion gives \(C_3\) exactly for \(a+2=3k^2\). Exact symbolic and finite checks in verify.py executed successfully, but are supplementary, not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The established 2026 parameter range is finite (a at most 1000) and its cubic theorem only gives necessary conditions for reducibility. The 2013 paper already owns the discriminant-square locus; the contribution is a new global root-exclusion theorem, hence unconditional complete cubic Galois classification for all nonnegative integers. Searched the exact unbounded irreducibility claim, its integer-root reduction, polynomial aliases and old stronger work without finding a prior covering proof. Unindexed equivalent argument remains possible.

value.rationale: Uniform \(n=3\) irreducibility removes the finite parameter cutoff of a contemporary theorem at the first degree beyond the naturally reducible \(n=2\) case. It yields a complete \(C_3\) versus \(S_3\) dichotomy for infinitely many members of both types, explicitly acknowledging that the discriminant square-locus was known in 2013. This is a natural complete classification, not an arbitrary numerical slice.
